summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload at npm install
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts the `bun` binary to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the local `math_init.js` file. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated bundle (rotated string-array construction, numeric-index lookup tables, non-semantic identifiers such as `MmgoCP`, `etDiOOB`, `WV8StW`, and a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header requiring the freshly dropped Bun runtime to execute it). This runs automatically on `npm install` via the preinstall lifecycle hook, executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine through a runtime chosen specifically to bypass Node-based inspection. The obfuscated payload is unrelated to the package's advertised purpose (a React marketing-form helper). The `@servicetitan/marketing-form` name and `servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib` repo reference present as first-party ServiceTitan tooling, but the shipped preinstall dropper and Bun-only obfuscated bundle alongside a small amount of genuine React helper code are consistent with scope impersonation rather than a legitimate first-party release.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
